title: LocalStack for Azure Enters Public Preview with Security Settings Stored but Not Enforced
gist: LocalStack's Azure emulator is now in free, self-serve public preview, with general availability expected in early 2027. It runs existing ARM/Bicep, Terraform, Pulumi and Azure CLI deployments locally across a broad list of services. The product's own documentation shows partial API coverage (for example, 13 of 81 Storage Account operations) and many security and network settings that are stored but not enforced, so insecure configurations pass locally, including for AI agents testing in the sandbox.

insights.claim: LocalStack's Azure emulator is in free, self-serve public preview, with general availability expected in early 2027. Pricing arrives at GA and preview access ends then, but the transition terms are not settled: the product page still shows "[30 days]" as a literal placeholder.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Early adopters face pricing and transition terms that have not been decided yet.
insights.quote: the product page still carries "[30 days]" as a literal placeholder and an unfilled next-steps section
insights.locator: Developer experience features, including App Inspector

insights.claim: The emulator accepts existing ARM and Bicep templates, Terraform modules, Pulumi programs and Azure CLI scripts without rewrites. It covers services including AKS, Container Apps, Functions, App Service, Cosmos DB, Service Bus, Event Hubs, Key Vault and API Management, and gives each developer an isolated sandbox for development and testing, not as a replacement for Azure.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Running cloud tests locally could cut Azure dev-subscription costs and slow iteration loops.
insights.quote: without waiting on a dev subscription or paying for every iteration.

insights.claim: Microsoft's own local tools (Azurite for Blob/Queue/Table storage, the Cosmos DB emulator and Azure Functions Core Tools) do not combine into one environment where an ARM or Bicep deployment can run end to end. LocalStack aims to fill that gap.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: LocalStack is going after a gap in Microsoft's own developer tooling.
insights.locator: Microsoft’s own local tooling is narrower

insights.claim: The project is led by Paolo Salvatori, a 28-year Microsoft principal and creator of Service Bus Explorer. He frames the fidelity promise this way: if a solution works on Azure but fails on the emulator, that is LocalStack's bug.
insights.speaker: Paolo Salvatori
insights.so_what: The promise covers only false failures, not false passes.
insights.quote: If your solution runs perfectly on Azure but fails on our emulator, that is our bug to fix.
insights.locator: If your solution runs perfectly on

insights.claim: The documentation covers 24 resource providers and reports partial API implementation: Storage Accounts covers 13 of 81 operations, App Service 143 of 616, and Virtual Network 10 of 29.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Most of the Azure API surface is still unimplemented, so teams should check coverage before relying on it.
insights.quote: Storage Accounts covers 13 of 81 operations. App Service covers 143 of 616. Virtual Network covers 10 of 29.

themes.theme: Stored-but-not-enforced security settings create false passes

insights.claim: Configuration is often accepted, stored and returned without taking effect. On App Service, keys, access restrictions, authentication settings and publishing credential policies are not enforced, httpsOnly is ignored and the app serves HTTP, and VNet integration has no network effect.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Tests can pass security configurations that would behave differently, or be blocked, in real Azure.
insights.quote: Keys, access restrictions, authentication settings, and publishing credential policies are not enforced.

insights.claim: The emulator does not route network traffic or enforce security rules. Peering is unsupported, and VPN gateways, ExpressRoute, Load Balancer, Application Gateway and Network Watcher are not implemented.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Network-security designs cannot be tested meaningfully in the emulator.
insights.quote: the emulator does not route network traffic or enforce security rules

insights.claim: In Storage, data-plane requests with any bearer token succeed unless RBAC enforcement is enabled. A user delegation SAS does not re-check RBAC, unsupported headers are silently accepted, and x-ms-version is not validated.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Authentication bugs can get through local testing unnoticed.
insights.quote: Data-plane requests with a bearer token succeed whenever a token is present unless RBAC enforcement is enabled.
insights.locator: Several Storage divergences land on authentication.

insights.claim: Salvatori's fidelity promise covers code that runs in Azure and fails locally, but the documented gaps mostly describe the reverse: misconfigurations pass locally and nothing in the run flags the difference.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Teams should treat a local pass as unverified for anything involving security or networking.
insights.quote: Both pass locally, and nothing in the run flags the difference.

insights.claim: LocalStack pitches the sandbox as a place for AI agents to "deploy, break, and retry" without live credentials. But an agent iterating there gets access restrictions stored rather than applied, and any bearer token accepted, and both come back as passes.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: AI agents trained or tested on the emulator may learn insecure configurations that look valid.

insights.claim: A web app created on a Windows plan runs in the Linux runtime. The Oryx build image ships for amd64 only, so on Apple Silicon code builds fail and apps start without dependencies. App Service state is held in memory and lost when the emulator stops.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Mac-based developer teams in particular will hit failures before they reach the deeper fidelity gaps.
insights.quote: A web app created on a Windows plan runs its code in the Linux runtime.
